title: Tribute to Professor Valmo Victor
summary: Kimball's schoolmate and teacher Valmo Victor, who taught many New Orleans musicians.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: Oh yeah, and this is something else that I'd like to go in the interview. I feel that I owe this to a friend of mine, because we started out as musicians together. And to be perfectly frank, the first organized group that I played in was in the high school orchestra. And Professor Valmo Victor, he's a retired school teacher now. He's still around now. He's still here in New Orleans. And it would be nice if you wouldn't interview him. Yeah, it would be nice if I could interview him. What is the whole name again now?
Would he be in the phone book?

I'm sure that he is. I'm sure that he is. He's responsible for many musicians, many good musicians. Lord Jack Willis that plays trumpet, he taught him to play music. Al Goodman, the bass player, you've heard of him? Heard of him, yeah. He's a very fine bass player. Another fellow that they called Foots is a drummer.
Oh yeah, I heard of him.

He was in that group. And many of the musicians who were playing with some big bands away from here now, they started under him as a teacher. Valmo and I were classmates. And he played the piano for the groups to sing. A boy named Hannibal played the violin. The two grand brothers, one played violin and the other played clarinet. And we had a little group that would play for little afternoon class parties. And I had my banjo. And we thought that we were something with that group that we had. But I always said that in the event that I should ever be interviewed, I would always feel as though I should pay a tribute to Valmo Victor because he definitely is a fine musician. And he plays all instruments. He taught all instruments.
He taught the music then in the schools too?

No, he didn't teach. We were schoolmates together. Then he was a school teacher. And then he had. He taught other subjects. Yeah, he taught literary subjects. But he had at his home, he taught many private lessons. And he had quite a few students that he thought were successful. So that's, I feel satisfied now that I've paid that tribute to him.
